title: Specification statements
description: Refinement calculus starts from specification statements — 'x : [pre, post]', meaning 'change x so that pre implies post' — and refines them step by step into executable code. Each step is proved correct; the final program is correct by construction, not by testing.
method: Write the spec statement; apply refinement laws (sequence, alternation, iteration introduction); prove each step's side conditions.
usage: Start from the spec statement; refine in small proved steps; never skip a side condition.

demo.code:
print('spec: x : [true, x = max(a,b)]')
print('refine: if a>=b -> x:=a [] a<b -> x:=b fi (alternation law)')
print('side conditions proved -> CORRECT')

title: Data refinement (representation change)
description: Data refinement swaps abstract data for concrete representation — a set spec becomes a sorted list implementation — via a coupling invariant linking them. Prove the coupling invariant is maintained and every abstract operation refines to concrete code; the representation change is invisible to clients.
method: Define the coupling invariant; refine each operation; prove the invariant is established and preserved.
usage: Write the coupling invariant explicitly; it's the heart of the data refinement.

demo.code:
print('abstract: set S; concrete: sorted list L')
print('coupling: set(L) = S and sorted(L)')
print('operations refined, invariant preserved -> clients unaffected')

title: Action systems refinement
description: Action systems (Back) model reactive programs as guarded actions on shared state; refinement adds detail while preserving observable behavior. It's refinement calculus for concurrency — the rely/guarantee reasoning integrates with stepwise development of parallel programs.
method: Specify as actions with guards; refine by decomposing actions and adding variables; prove each refinement step.
usage: Model the reactive core as actions; refine toward the implementation architecture.

demo.code:
print('action: transfer when funds available')
print('refined: +logging, +retry; observable behavior preserved -> proved')

title: Z notation schema refinement
description: Z specifies systems as schemas (state + operations as predicates); refinement in Z relates abstract and concrete schemas via retrieve relations. The Spivey/Wordsworth calculus gives the proof rules; the retrieve relation plays the coupling invariant's role.
method: Write abstract schemas; define the retrieve relation; prove operation refinement against it; compose refinements.
usage: Use Z where the spec is state-rich; keep retrieve relations simple and total where possible.

demo.code:
print('abstract: Booking; concrete: BookingDB')
print('retrieve: db reflects bookings; operations refined -> proved')

title: Probabilistic refinement
description: McIver-Morgan extended refinement to probabilistic programs: specs include probabilistic choice, and refinement preserves not just correctness but probability distributions over outcomes. Randomized algorithms get the same stepwise development with quantitative guarantees.
method: Specify with probabilistic choice; refine preserving expectation properties; prove quantitative bounds at each step.
usage: Use for randomized algorithms where the quantitative bound is the requirement.

demo.code:
print('spec: P(success) >= 0.99')
print('refined implementation: P(success) = 0.995 >= 0.99 -> QUANTITATIVE REFINEMENT HOLDS')

title: Refinement patterns catalog
description: Experienced refiners reuse patterns: 'introduce accumulator', 'strengthen invariant', 'split case analysis'. A catalog of named refinement patterns — each with its law applications and side conditions — turns refinement from art into engineering practice.
method: Match the development step to a catalog pattern; apply its law sequence; discharge its standard side conditions.
usage: Build the team's pattern catalog from completed developments; teach patterns, not just laws.

demo.code:
print('pattern: introduce accumulator')
print('laws: data refinement + loop introduction -> applied, side conditions proved')

title: B-Method industrial refinement
description: The B-Method took refinement to industry: Paris Metro Line 14 (driverless) and various railway signaling systems were developed in B, with 100,000+ proof obligations discharged. Abstract machines refine to implementations; Atelier B checks every step — refinement at a scale most methods never reach.
method: Write abstract machines; refine to concrete; prove with Atelier B; generate code from the final refinement.
usage: Use for safety-critical control; invest in proof automation for the obligation volume.

demo.code:
print('Metro L14: 86,000 proof obligations')
print('Atelier B: 99.2% automatic -> implementation proved, zero defects in service')

title: Event-B method
description: Event-B (Abrial) applies refinement to reactive systems: start with an abstract machine of events, refine through levels adding detail, proving each level refines the last. The Rodin platform discharges proof obligations; Paris Metro Line 14's safety software was developed this way.
method: Abstract machine -> refinement levels; prove guard strengthening and invariant preservation per level; Rodin manages obligations.
usage: Refine in small levels; keep each level's new detail minimal; let Rodin track obligations.

demo.code:
print('M0: abstract doors; M1: +sensors; M2: +timing')
print('Rodin: 214 obligations, 208 auto, 6 interactive -> all discharged')
